claims.text: IV when severe (ECG changes or severe Sx), unresponsive to oral tx, or in hospitalized pts on digoxin or w significant heart dz or ongoing losses
claims.quote: When hypokalemia is severe (eg, with ECG changes or severe symptoms), is unresponsive to oral therapy, or occurs in hospitalized patients who are taking digoxin or who have significant heart disease or ongoing losses, potassium must be replaced IV.

claims.text: Routine IV rate no more than 10 mEq/h; hypokalemic arrhythmia: up to 40 mEq/h via a central vein, only w continuous cardiac monitoring
claims.quote: For hypokalemic arrhythmia, give IV potassium chloride through a central vein at a maximum of 40 mEq (40 mmol)/hour and only with continuous cardiac monitoring; routine IV infusion should be no more than 10 mEq (10 mmol)/hour.

claims.text: Avoid dextrose/glucose diluent (insulin rise can transiently worsen hypokalemia)
claims.quote: Dextrose or glucose solutions used for dilution are avoided because elevation in the serum insulin concentrations could result in transient worsening of hypokalemia.

claims.text: W hypomagnesemia: correct both K and Mg
claims.quote: When hypokalemia occurs with hypomagnesemia, both the potassium and magnesium deficiencies must be corrected to stop ongoing renal potassium wasting.
